leaving in review a little longer to give folks time to object.

> 
> pr 18 17:23:48 p10bmc bmcweb[1099]: [ERROR async_resolve.hpp:92] Resolve failed: Connection timed out
> Apr 18 17:23:48 p10bmc bmcweb[1099]: [ERROR http_client.hpp:179] Resolve failed: Connection timed out https://9.5.5.122:80/redfish/v1/AggregationService/AggregationSources

Adding clarification in case others may think this is a bug.  `/redfish/v1` requires querying any satellite BMCs in case we need to add links to resource collection which do not appear on the aggregating BMC but do appear on a satellite BMC.

The timeout is thus because the aggregator has to timeout while waiting for a response from a BMC that does not exist.

We'll hit a failure if we try to add a satellite HMC through POST when one already exists on dbus.  Same for adding multiple satellites through POST.

Should we add handling to prevent these cases in the POST handler or add a check in the aggregator to avoid searching dbus (and hitting this check) if the `currentAggregationSources` unordered_map is not empty?

> We'll hit a failure if we try to add a satellite HMC through POST when one already exists on dbus.  Same for adding multiple satellites through POST.
> 
> Should we add handling to prevent these cases in the POST handler or add a check in the aggregator to avoid searching dbus (and hitting this check) if the `currentAggregationSources` unordered_map is not empty?


For the moment that's intentional, because we only have one prefix defined, so even if this condition wasn't present, we'd still fail later on.  We still only support one aggregation source at a time, although it'd be great to fix that, I'd rather keep this specific patch as "only supports one satmc" and work on supporting multiples in a future patch.  Seem ok?

> We still only support one aggregation source at a time, although it'd be great to fix that, I'd rather keep this specific patch as "only supports one satmc" and work on supporting multiples in a future patch. Seem ok?

Yeah I'm good with that as long as it's understood that this new POST support can cause breakages.  It may be helpful to call out in the commit that aggregation is still only supported for a single satellite BMC total regardless of if it's added via POST or dbus.
Added to the commit message.
This will need to be updated since the satellites added via POST will get randomized prefixes.
Yep..... it will if we support more than one sat at a time.  Pretty sure for a single sat it's correct?

I don't think it's correct if that single sat is added by POST.  Its key will be a randomized 8 character string instead of "5B247A".  The "5B247A" we use is hardcoded inside of the `findSatelliteConfigs()` and that's only for sats detected via dbus.

What would happen is you'd see aggregated resources listed when you query top level collections like `/redfish/v1/Chassis`, but then if you tried to actually query the aggregated resource then you'll get a 404 NOT FOUND because this check will fail and the aggregator won't forward the request.

One of these options should work for the short term:
1. Change POST to always use "5B247A" since we're still only supporting a single satellite BMC for now
2. Use the key from the new map if it's not empty and fall back to "5B247A" if it is.

Longer term it'd be something like one of these options:
1. Retrieve all satellite configs before this comparison
2. Cache dbus satellite configs in the new map and iterate over its keys here

How does this get turned off ? Like a normal POST on a resource if you don't support it in the backend, the backend app can return something like "Not supported", bmcweb could return that.. but this is purely a bmcweb concept. Let's say you want aggregation but not allow clients to create aggregation (idk, maybe this would be an weird corner use case?)

> the backend app can return something like "Not supported"

In redfish you would generally do this by just not populating the appropriate tree.  In this case, AggregationSources.  I'm not sure where we'd return not supported, can you elaborate a little?

> Let's say you want aggregation but not allow clients to create aggregation

If there's a case where this exists (you want to disallow something), we could add a meson flag to remove "dynamic" support, but I don't think anyone needs that yet?
I'm okay with this
